- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially when sentiment > 0.75 and recent prices are rising.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or corrections when sentiment drops below 0.5 and prices show mean reversion.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts when sentiment is low (e.g., < 0.4) and recent price action shows downward momentum.
- Reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% if sentiment is weak (e.g., < 0.6) and true price has shown persistent downward drift.
- Correct for lagged overreaction: if model forecasts peak 2–3 days after sentiment peak, reduce forecast by 10–15% to align with true price’s slower decay.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average and sentiment is neutral or declining, reduce forecast by 5–8%.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after 3+ consecutive days of downward price action, even if sentiment is rising — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent low.
